questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of an entrepreneur?
options: A person who identifies an opportunity, organises resources to exploit it and takes the financial risk
Any person employed by a business
A manager who organises and controls existing resources
A person who lends money to new businesses
questions.why: The four parts of the role are spotting the opportunity, organising the resources, taking the risk and making the decisions. Naming them beats talking vaguely about risk-taking.
whyNot: An employee does not take the financial risk or organise the venture.
That is management. An entrepreneur creates the venture rather than administering one.
That is an investor or lender, who supplies finance without running the business.

questions.stem: Which term is defined as: entrepreneurial behaviour by an employee within an existing business?
options: Intrapreneurship
Entrepreneurship
Social entrepreneurship
Management
questions.why: An intrapreneur develops new ideas using the company's resources, so they get to innovate without taking the personal financial risk.
whyNot: Entrepreneurship means setting up the venture yourself and bearing the risk.
Social entrepreneurship is about a social purpose, which is a different distinction.
Management organises existing activity rather than creating new.

questions.stem: Which of these is the most commonly cited barrier to starting a business?
options: Lack of finance
Too many available opportunities
An excess of business skills
Low levels of competition
questions.why: Lenders want security and a track record, and a start-up has neither, so finance is usually the binding constraint.
whyNot: Opportunities are not a barrier, and too many would be a pleasant problem.
A lack of skills is a barrier; an excess is not.
Low competition makes entry easier, not harder.

questions.stem: Why do large businesses want to encourage intrapreneurship?
options: It produces innovation without the employee bearing the personal financial risk, and keeps ambitious staff
It reduces the wage bill immediately
It removes the need for any management structure
It guarantees that new products succeed
questions.why: The company gets new ideas developed with its own resources, and the ambitious people who might otherwise leave to start something themselves have a reason to stay.
whyNot: It usually costs money: budget and time have to be protected for it.
It needs a structure that deliberately protects small teams from normal approval processes.
Nothing guarantees a new product will succeed.

questions.stem: Why is intrapreneurship difficult to achieve in a large organisation?
options: Budgets, procedures and approval processes are designed to prevent unplanned activity
Large organisations have no resources
Employees in large firms have no ideas
It is prohibited by company law
questions.why: The controls that make a large business efficient are exactly what stop an employee experimenting. Making intrapreneurship work means deliberately exempting small teams from them.
whyNot: They have far more resources than a start-up, which is the attraction.
An unsupported claim about people.
There is no such legal restriction.

questions.stem: A would-be entrepreneur has savings of $8,000 and needs $40,000 to start. Which barrier binds?
options: Finance
Lack of ideas
Excessive regulation
Lack of competition
questions.why: The gap between what they have and what they need is the constraint, and quoting those two figures is exactly the application an examiner is looking for.
whyNot: They evidently have an idea, since they have costed it.
Regulation may also be a barrier, but nothing in the figures points to it.
Low competition would help them, not hinder them.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of a business plan when approaching a bank?
options: To show the business is viable and persuade the lender to provide finance
To guarantee the business will succeed
To satisfy a legal requirement for all new businesses
To replace the need for market research
questions.why: A plan sets out the market, the operations and the financial forecasts so a lender can judge the risk. It also forces the founder to test their own assumptions in writing.
whyNot: No plan guarantees success, and saying so is a good evaluation point.
Business plans are not generally a legal requirement.
The plan is built ON market research; it does not replace it.

questions.stem: Which of these should an entrepreneur manage through flexibility rather than insurance?
options: Uncertainty, such as a sudden halt to international travel
A predictable seasonal fall in demand
The known percentage of stock that is damaged each year
An expected annual rise in wages
questions.why: Uncertainty cannot have a probability attached, so it cannot be insured or forecast. It is handled by keeping cash, avoiding long fixed commitments and planning for more than one scenario.
whyNot: Seasonality repeats and can be forecast, so it is a risk that can be planned for.
A measurable rate from past data is a risk, and it can be insured.
An expected cost rise is foreseeable and can be budgeted for.

questions.stem: Which phase of the entrepreneurial role do founders most commonly find difficult?
options: Running and expanding the business day to day
Spotting the original opportunity
Writing the initial business plan
Registering the business
questions.why: Starting is exciting; operating is discipline. Cash flow, staff, quality and customers day after day need different skills from the ones that spotted the opportunity, which is the same transition as entrepreneur to leader.
whyNot: Founders are usually good at this; it is why they started.
Demanding but one-off, and help is widely available.
An administrative step rather than the hard part.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a barrier to entrepreneurship?
options: Fear of failure, particularly where business failure carries a lasting stigma
A large potential market
Access to cheap premises
Support from a business network
questions.why: Where failing in business is socially costly, fewer people attempt it at all. It is a genuine barrier and one that varies a great deal between countries.
whyNot: A large market is an opportunity, not a barrier.
Cheap premises reduce the finance barrier.
Networks help overcome barriers.
